bull_bear.body:
- World's largest zinc-lead mine at Rampura Agucha, India, with Zinc India R&R of 468.6 million tonnes and mine life of 25+ years
- Largest Integrated producer of Zinc and among the top 10 producers of silver globally
- Largest aluminium production capability in India at 2.44 MTPA, with largest capacity in India and targeted to be 3rd largest globally (ex-China) post expansion
- One of India's largest private sector crude oil producers, with total acreage of >47,000 sq km across India and gross 2P & 2C R&R of 1,321 mmboe
- One of the largest producers and exporters of iron ore in India, and one of the largest producers and exporters of merchant pig iron
- One of the largest copper production capacities in India
- Cost leadership: zinc cost of production at a 5-year low of US$959/MT (down 9% Y-o-Y); aluminium hot metal cost at a 5-year low of US$1,752/t
- Integrated infrastructure moat: world's longest continuously heated pipeline (Barmer to Gujarat coast, ~670 km) for oil transport
- Diversified, tier-1 asset base across India, Africa and the Middle East spanning the full value chain from exploration to value-addition
- ESG leadership/reputation: Hindustan Zinc ranked #1 in S&P Global CSA for the 3rd consecutive year and Vedanta Aluminium ranked 2nd among peers; Oil & Gas business ranked top-5 globally in its first participation
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price and currency/interest-rate volatility — Company explicitly flags uncertainty arising from the behaviour of financial and metals markets including the London Metal Exchange, and fluctuations in interest and/or exchange rates and metal prices, as a driver that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements.
- Broad external, political, regulatory and environmental exposure — Forward-looking statements are explicitly qualified by uncertainties of national, regional and global scale, including environmental, climatic, natural, political, economic, business, competitive and regulatory nature, reflecting Vedanta's multi-jurisdiction (India, South Africa, Middle East) operating footprint.
- Acquisition integration risk — Future integration of acquired businesses is explicitly named as a source of uncertainty that could cause actual results to differ from expectations.
- Structural demerger execution/transition risk — Capital allocation and investment decisions are being made in the context of an ongoing strategic demerger of the Group into five independent, sector-specific, pure-play companies, introducing organisational transition and execution risk.
- Cybersecurity risk — The Company's Risk Management Policy (revised 2019) explicitly covers cybersecurity, indicating it is treated as a principal enterprise risk category within the Group Risk Governance Framework alongside external, strategic, financial and operational risks.
- Concentration on the Indian demand/economic cycle — Vedanta positions itself as India's largest diversified natural resources company, with its demand outlook and growth thesis explicitly tied to Indian real GDP growth (7.3% in FY 2025-26, ~6.8% estimated for the current year) and government capital outlay/infrastructure initiatives, making performance sensitive to the Indian macro and policy cycle.
- Inherent operational risk of global natural-resources operations — The Group's businesses operate in a dynamic environment and are exposed to a range of risks inherent to a global natural resources organisation spanning mining, smelting and oil & gas across multiple geographies, requiring a multi-layered risk management framework with structured risk appetite statements and quantitative thresholds introduced this year.

business.body: Vedanta operates across the full natural-resources value chain -- exploration, asset development, extraction, processing and value-addition -- in zinc-lead-silver, iron ore, steel, copper, aluminium, power, nickel and oil and gas, holding market-leading positions in several of these businesses. It serves industrial consumers in automotive, steel, power generation, infrastructure, battery manufacturing and oil, supplying primary metals as well as value-added products such as sheets, rods, bars and rolled products across zinc, aluminium and copper. The Company is also transitioning toward critical minerals, energy transition/clean energy and electronics/display-glass manufacturing under its 'Vedanta 2.0' strategy.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Zinc-Lead-Silver:** Zinc metal, Lead metal, Silver metals and bars, Value-added zinc/lead/silver products, EcoZen (low-carbon zinc)
- **Aluminium:** Aluminium ingots, Wire rods, Primary foundry alloy, Rolled products, Billet, Slab, Alumina (calcined)
- **Copper:** Copper cathode
- **Oil & Gas:** Crude oil, Natural gas
- **Iron Ore:** Saleable iron ore (DMT), Pig iron
- **Steel:** Pig iron, Billets, TMT bars, Wire rods, Ductile iron pipes
- **Ferro Alloys (FACOR):** High Carbon Ferrochrome
- **Power:** Merchant power (thermal)
- **Emerging:** Display/electronics glass (foray)

outlook.body:
- Vedanta 2.0: strategic transformation repositioning the portfolio toward energy transition, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing and clean technologies, while harnessing AI, automation and innovation for agility and future-readiness
- S1: Championing world-class ESG performance
- S2: Augment Reserves & Resources (R&R) base responsibly
- S3: Delivering growth opportunities
- S4: Optimise capital allocation and maintain a strong balance sheet
- S5: Operational excellence and cost leadership
- Completed demerger into five independent, sector-specific, pure-play companies to unlock shareholder value, sharpen strategy and strengthen capital structures of each business
- Backward/vertical integration to secure raw materials (coal, bauxite) within ~100 km of plants, targeting 100% coal security and stronger bauxite security
- Diversifying into newer critical minerals -- nickel, chromium, cobalt, vanadium, manganese, tungsten, gold and rare earth elements -- to tap future industrial, technology and digital applications
- Shift toward higher-margin value-added products (VAP) across businesses -- e.g. Aluminium VAP output raised to 60% of production; ESL Steel targeting 100% VAP production via conceptual study for full hot-metal-to-VAP conversion
- FACOR vision to become India's largest Ferrochrome producer by FY 2028-29 via three pivotal projects (greenfield smelter, underground mine, concentrator)
- Cairn Oil & Gas aspires to contribute 50% of India's domestic Oil & Gas production through technology-based exploration success and integrated development
- Vedanta Nicomet strategic expansion to strengthen domestic nickel capability and reduce import dependence, aligned with Atma Nirbhar Bharat and government critical-minerals incentives
- Disciplined capital allocation to support sustainable growth, maintain a strong balance sheet and generate robust free cash flow, with continued deleveraging
- Company describes a consistent dividend track record as a sign of sustained growth and a means of equitably sharing economic value for widespread socioeconomic welfare; three interim dividends were declared and paid during FY 2025-26 with no final dividend recommended. Capital Allocation Policy states the Company has always strived to maintain optimal capital allocation to strengthen the balance sheet, with an approach of growing sustainably and with financial prudence, guided by principles forming part of a formal Capital Allocation Policy.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Hindustan Zinc (HZL) is progressing toward a 2 MTPA integrated metal capacity: the 160 KTPA Debari roaster has been commissioned; a hot-acid-leaching lead-silver recovery plant at Dariba (adding 27 TPA silver and 6 KTPA lead) is expected complete by Q1 FY 2026-27; cellhouse debottlenecking at Dariba Smelting Complex and Chanderiya Lead-Zinc Smelter added 21 KTPA metal capacity; the Bamnia Kalan mine project is under excavation (box-cut of portal); a 510 KTPA fertiliser plant is targeted for Q2 FY 2026-27; the Board (June 2025) approved a 250 KTPA integrated refined-zinc capacity expansion with associated mining/milling, EPC partners locked in, targeted for Q2 FY 2028-29; the Board (August 2025) approved India's first zinc tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha (10 MTPA feed capacity), EPC locked in, targeted Q4 FY 2027-28; and the Board (January 2026) approved exploration capex aimed at raising metal reserves from ~13 MnT to 50 MnT, primarily via the Zawar and Rajpura Dariba clusters, to sustain a 25+ year mine life. The 250 KTPA expansion and tailings plant form Phase 1 of an overall plan to double capacity; Phase 2 projects are yet to be announced. In Aluminium, the Company -- already India's largest primary producer -- targets 3 MTPA smelting capacity by FY 2027-28 with 100% backward vertical integration; Environmental Clearance has been recommended for the Sijimali bauxite block (~310 million tonne reserve) with mining expected to start Q1 FY 2026-27; the Lanjigarh refinery expansion from 2 to 5 MTPA is commissioned (Train-1 alumina from March 2024, Train-2 from October 2025), with full ramp-up expected by FY 2026-27; and BALCO's 0.435 MTPA smelter project achieved first metal on 6 October 2025 from India's highest 525 kA smelter, alongside a 50 KTPA Wire Rod Mill, 90 KTPA Primary Foundry Alloy line and half of a 424 KTPA Billet line, with full completion targeted next financial year to take BALCO to 1 MTPA aluminium (4th-largest single-site ex-China). In coal, Jamkhani is at approved capacity, Kuraloi A North is expected online Q1 FY 2026-27, Ghogharpalli Q3 FY 2026-27, and Barra is in the pipeline, aimed at 100% coal security. At Vedanta Zinc International, the 200 KTPA Gamsberg Phase-II expansion (Northern Cape, South Africa) is in the construction-finishing/commissioning phase (93.7% complete), targeting water trials/initial ore charging in July 2026 and full ramp-up by September 2026, taking total MIC capacity from 300 to 500 KTPA. Separately, the Company has begun more actively monetising surplus real estate accumulated through past acquisitions, and is evaluating options to unlock further value from these real estate holdings.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is in the middle of a multi-decade economic expansion set to become the world's growth epicentre, with unparalleled infrastructure creation, industrialisation, rising energy demand and energy transition -- each fundamentally metal-intensive, creating structural long-term domestic demand for minerals
- Portfolio resilience stems from diversification, vertical integration and domestic demand exposure -- 15+ commodities primarily consumed within India provide resilience against global uncertainty
- Backward integration and cost leadership reduce vulnerability to commodity price volatility; disciplined hedging approach provides cashflow certainty and downside protection while retaining upside exposure
- FY 2025-26 was a tale of two halves: H1 saw tariff-related uncertainty and Middle East/Europe conflict-driven turbulence in commodity markets; demand for metals and energy strengthened with prices remaining favourable as the year progressed, with a sharp rise in commodity prices in H2
- Strong Indian economic growth alongside infrastructure, manufacturing and energy-transition investment ensured steady domestic demand for minerals
- Focus on completing capex and debottlenecking projects across aluminium, zinc, oil & gas and power to improve volumes
- Productivity gains via predictive maintenance, analytics and operational excellence measures in existing capacity
- Cost of production reduction driven by economies of scale, enhanced captive power utilisation, raw material sourcing optimisation and shift toward higher-margin value-added products
- Deleveraging and prudent capital allocation optimised borrowing costs, supporting Net Debt/EBITDA improvement to 0.95x
- Power business sales volume growth driven by new capacity addition at Meenakshi and Athena, despite demand moderation in some regions due to the monsoon
- Oil & Gas exploration portfolio spans 44 blocks, with FY 2026-27 capex earmarked for near-term volume initiatives (ASP Injection at Mangala, tight-oil drilling, onshore/offshore exploration)
- Growth-project pipeline across businesses: Zinc India smelting capacity expansion (1.14 to 1.38 MTPA) and zinc tailings reprocessing plant; Gamsberg Phase-II (nearing completion) and Phase-III (aspirational); BALCO 1 MTPA aluminium completion; FACOR 330 KTPA ferrochrome smelter, 1.5 MTPA underground mine and 600 KTPA concentrator; ESL Steel 3.5 MTPA hot-metal expansion; coal mine ramp-ups at Kuraloi A North, Ghogharpalli and Barra; copper 155 KTPA rod mill at Ras-Al-Khair, Saudi Arabia; Nicomet proposed 50 KTPA nickel refinery
- Cairn Oil & Gas drilled 46 new wells during FY 2025-26 to sustain production growth, with Deep Gas drilling, Tight Oil drilling and exploration success at Ambe (Greater Ambe area and OALP-IX blocks) supporting an accelerated development pipeline

sk.overview: The sector covers the environmentally responsible recovery and recycling of end-of-life energy storage products (principally used lead-acid batteries) and non-ferrous scrap into pure lead and lead alloys — a circular-economy activity that reclaims critical resources from waste streams. meta.thesis: Vedanta Limited, a subsidiary of Vedanta Resources Limited, is a global natural resources conglomerate with a diversified, tier-1 portfolio spanning zinc-lead-silver, iron ore, steel, copper, aluminium, power, nickel and oil and gas, with strategic assets across India, Africa and the Middle East.
